images.title: Two negatives make positive, three make negative
images.purpose: Compares (−6)² = 36, which is positive, with (−6)³ = −216, which is negative.
images.composition: Plain white background, the main object large and centred with wide empty margins, no scenery, no characters, no extra decoration. Two panels side by side: two tokens on the left, three tokens on the right, each with one result below.
images.exact_structure: Left panel: exactly 2 round tokens each reading −6, filled vermilion (#D55E00), in a row; below them (−6)² = 36 with a teal (#0072B2) tag positive. Right panel: exactly 3 round tokens each reading −6, filled vermilion (#D55E00), in a row; below them (−6)³ = −216 with a vermilion (#D55E00) tag negative. A thin grey (#6B7280) vertical divider between the panels. Nothing else in the frame.
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec

images.takeaway: The cube of a negative number is negative, while its square is positive.
images.description: Compares (−6)² = 36, which is positive, with (−6)³ = −216, which is negative.

image_decisions.why: A side by side count of negative factors shows why the sign flips between square and cube.
